HIST-103.consensus:
STRENGTHS: Students consistently describe Dr. O'Neill as passionate and engaging — lectures use multimedia (Monty Python clips, movie trailers, humor) that make a GE history class feel lively rather than dry. Many say the content is genuinely interesting if you show up and pay attention.

GRADING & WORKLOAD: Mixed reviews on grading — several note she can be a harsh essay grader and that strong discussion participation matters. Expect substantial section readings; essays benefit from office-hours or TA help. Low-weight pop quizzes (~5% total) sometimes used to track attendance.

BOTTOM LINE: Solid pick for students who engage in class and discussion; less ideal if you want a low-effort GE or struggle with writing-heavy assessments.

BUAD-281.consensus:
STRENGTHS: Very high marks for personality and support — students call Prof. Braunegg kind, funny, caring, and responsive by email. Daily accounting facts/jokes are a recurring positive. Many praise his career advice and willingness to help outside class; several credit him with influencing their major choice.

TEACHING & EXAMS: More divided on in-class instruction — some say he struggles to work through problems live or that lectures don't always align with exams. Course draws on Prof. Layton's materials but sections may not match perfectly. Textbook gets criticism.

BOTTOM LINE: Strong human connection and mentorship; be prepared to self-study or use tutors if lecture pace doesn't click. High would-take-again despite polarized exam/lecture comments.

BUAD-304.consensus:
STRENGTHS: Among the most praised Marshall professors on RMP — repeatedly called the 'best' or 'sweetest' instructor students have had. Negotiation and OB classes get standout reviews: supportive classroom culture, clear and organized Brightspace, strong lectures, and generous extra credit. Weekly in-class negotiations are a highlight for many.

WORKLOAD: Group projects and class participation carry real weight; some find readings or lecture content repetitive. A few note group work can feel heavy even when the professor is beloved.

BOTTOM LINE: Take her if you can — especially for negotiation-heavy offerings. Show up, participate, and lean into the structured group work; exams reward attentive note-taking on lecture and slide content.

ECON-351.consensus:
STRENGTHS: Reviewers repeatedly praise board work, step-by-step problem breakdowns, and practice sets that mirror exams. Many call him kind, funny, and responsive by email; office hours and TAs get strong mentions. Several note you can succeed without mandatory attendance if you self-study from the textbook.

COMMON CAVEATS: Spanish accent and fast lecture pace come up often — sit near the front. Some say lectures/textbook do not fully prepare you unless you drill mock exams and homework. Content volume is high; procrastination hurts.

EXAMS & GRADING: Midterms align with practice problems and mock exams; homework is described as easy/lenient (best-of policy). Grades span A to C- depending on effort. AI/group project mentioned as straightforward when you keep up.

BOTTOM LINE: Do the practice sets, use TAs/office hours, and do not fall behind — accent and pace are manageable with front-row seating and self-study.

reviews.comment: The tests are easy if you just do the practice sets. He's great at explanations.

personally the class is hard, because there is a lot of content. do not procrastinate it will be your downfall. midterms are the same as mock exams and homework, so just practice that. group project at end is straightforward, homework is easy. ultimately your grade depends on your own effort so try!!

Alejandro is very nice and sometimes his accent is hard to understand in lecture but overall you understand what he is saying. The tests are exactly like the practice problems and he's very funny. Do the practice and you will do well in class!

His lectures are enjoyable and structures the class to be very flexible with no required attendance and lenient homework policies. He does however have a spanish accent which makes understading lecture difficult sometimes. Additonally, I felt the lectures and textbook do not adequately prepare you for exams.

Really great professor, he writes on the board with practice questions, so concepts are easier to follow. He has an excellent TA who goes through all the questions, is super understanding and helpful, and she explains concepts really well. He has an accent, but it did not hinder my ability to learn. Definitely self-study as well, with the textbook!

Amazing professor. Has an accent but you get used to it. Can go through material pretty quickly, but he writes on board and explains while demonstrating, which helps a lot. He also goes back to explain if students are still confused. Exams are relatively the same as practice problems he gives.

GREAT PROFESSOR. He breaks down the steps of each problem amazingly, accent is a little thick (sit in the front it helps a lot), His office hours are worth it, he will make sure you understand!! Work hard from the beginning and do ALL practice problems (repeats in test).

Its a hard class and his lectures go by quick. With that being said he is really good at teaching and also really accessible outside of class. Answers emails extremely quickly and grades test within a few days of the test date. Exams are hard, but if you study and go to an office hour before the test your fine.

Professor flies through the lectures and his accent makes it difficult to understand and keep up. The course is already known for being a tough course. When questions are asked he sort of laughs and makes you feel bad before explaining. He has really good TAs though that help you step by step. I would definitely go to office hours.
- Genuinely moves at the speed of light - Is accessible outside of class, but truly have to grind for an A - Exams are super hard, homeworks are free - Professor is a bit condescending but means well
His accent and super fast pace of the class/lecture make it so hard to understand. The class is already hard and the speed of the lectures make this so hard

He does talk fast but if you don't understand or need to hear concept again he will gladly explain it to you until you get it. Very nice wants you to get an A but Econ isn't an easy class. Office hours are great way to prepare for test. Study guides very similar to exams.
Fantastic Professor. Easy looking at. Funny guy. Muy bien

Talks too fast and is hard to understand because of his accent. He mostly reads off the slides. But fun classes and passionate lecturer who encourages questions. He also uses real life examples which is useful.

Bro talks so fast, literally I was better off teaching it to myself outside of class. EXTREMELY condescending. I would go to his office hours and he would laugh at certain students questions and belittle them. Idk how his rating is so high, I'd drop if it weren't already to late in the semester.
no glaze, he's a really good professor and explained concepts very well. Would take him again every single time if I could choose.
Best professor I've had at USC. Took his econ351 class in fall 2024 and learned so much. Class is on Marshall curve so its competitive to get an A, but it wasn't that hard.

ECON 351 is a hard class no matter what, but if you have to take it def take Professor Martinez. Funny guy, doesn't mind explaining over and over again and has great lecture slides. Great TAs and curve. Tests are hard but they are no matter who you take. Hosts lots of reviews and genuinely cares and wants to hear our perspectives. Miss him!

This was my favorite professor of all time. In fact, the best professor I have ever had in my academic career. I highly recommend him. He makes lectures so fun. The class is hard, but if you understand calculus then you will ace the course. Highly recommend.

I am not sure why his reviews are so high... I was barely able to get a B- in this class after studying over 10 hours for each test. The practice tests were only somewhat similar and the homework took a lot of time. I would not recommend this teacher unless you want to go to office hours every week and try to get him to like you.
He's so easy to look at… take him

He is amazing. Went into 351 being really scared but honestly this class was way easier than I thought it would be. As long as you do all the practice problems and homework, there's no reason why you shouldn't get an A as tests are 95% similar to what you've seen before. For those complaining, they were just lazy and didn't do the work.

office hours with the TA saved me as his were completely full all the time. lectures were organized but he went so fast with explanations and skipped many steps making it confusing. only graded on 3 tests no curve and they are very difficult and only 24 points so very hard to get a good grade

His lectures were very confusing, and he taught so quickly. If you go to HIS office hours, he'll give you all the answers to homework and practice tests, which was nice, but his tests were very hard. He does not curve at all, so expect your grade to be heavily based on how you perform on the tests.

BEST PROF FOR ECON351. Tests are exactly what's on hw & practice sets. Lots of office hours. He let us go to any of his lectures (no attendance taken) + recordings posted online. He's great at explaining and his class makes econ fun/interesting. No complaints at all, very fair/interesting/funny guy. He wants you to get an A! TAKE HIM, TRUST.
Awesome professor. Lectures are interesting and exams are very similar to practice tests.

Good professor, but I would not take him again. he puts "trick questions" on exams so no one ends up getting them right. He switches up the questions on exams and they are way harder. I never put so much work into a class and I only got a B+ and thats with a 10 point curve so in reality my grade should be lower.

goat. 351 is hard but he makes it interesting and manageable. 3 exams each worth 30% and the other 10% is homework. go to lecture, do the practice problems and if you're still struggling read the textbook or go to office hours. take his class to get an A in econ and to laugh because he's hilarious.
Amazing professor! He includes real-world applications, which helps with understanding. And, I thought the class aligned with what he shared on the first day. Overall could not recommend more!

Goat. Simple as that. Gives plenty of practice tests/problems that are identical in concept and form to the actual tests. Just be aware that the bar for an A-range grade may change throughout the semester (i.e. A-range = >80 to A-range = >85).

Best teacher for microeconomics. Explains concepts well and is very clear about what will be on exams. Practice exams and chapter questions are identical to what will be on the tests. He's also super caring and will take the time to help you out and answer questions. By far my favorite professor this semester!

Professor Alejandro is one of my favorite and best professors in Marshall! He is so engaging and incorporated lots of humor into his lectures (which attendance was not mandatory for). It's also evident that he wants his students to do well and holds many office hours for studnets. Would totally take him again. THE GOAT 🐐
Professor Alejandro is awesome. His lecture is inspirational and well-explained. I love the vibe of his class, and the tests are always easy as long as you finish the sample problems.

If you attend classes and office hours, you will understand all concepts. The class isn't too bad especially if you did IB Econ. Just do the homework and practice tests, and you're good. His papers are also not too bad so if you practice well you will do well.

Best 351 prof he's so nice!!! Midterms are exactly like practice tests given. Homework is completion as long as you get half right and he gives you answers in office hours. Don't need to go to class-- he posts lectures and doesn't take attendance. Do the practice problems twice before the 3 tests and you can get an A. 80 or above overall is an A.

It's definitely a difficult class and you have to study A LOT for tests, but he holds office hours every day for the entire semester and gives a bunch of practice problems prior to midterms. The homework isn't too bad, but the difficulty of the class is dependent on whether or not you go to lectures. He overall made a difficult class digestible.
Exam questions are very similar to the practice sets he provides. Wants you to do well.

Such a great professor his class is so manageable. I barely went to lecture and never went to office hours and did perfectly fine. Homework is graded very easily and basically every single possible midterm question is provided to you between all the practice sets. Do all the questions and you'll be fine. By far the best choice for 351.

Great course if you show up to every lecture and pay attention. Taking notes, reviewing practice problems, and going to office hours when I needed help with certain problems made the class not overly difficult. Great lecturer and cares about his students. Would take him again if I could.

I never went to his office hours and skipped around 70% of classes and still got a decent grade. He is a good lecturer and grades aren't hard to get. PLEASE do practice questions because exam questions are 80% based on them.

Marquina made ECON351 a breeze. His lectures are straightforward, engaging, and explain the material well. Your grade is determined by 3 tests spaced out throughout the semester. They're non-cumulative which is nice. Do the homework and the exam practice sets and you'll get a top grade.

Makes microeconomics easy and provides fun examples for students to engage with. Do the homework and the practice midterms/final he provides to study and you will get an A in this class. Provides really, really helpful office hours for questions on homework and allows test revision. GOATED Marshall professor.

Great professor, but a fast lecturer. Overall would highly recommend him for Econ 351. The course is graded on only 3 written exams and weekly homework assignments, and as long as you do the practice questions he posts before each exam, they should be quite easy.

Despite being a new prof, Alejandro is a really engaging and fun lecturer. He's accessible and will help you perform your best in class as long as you put in the work. I love him and would take his classes again. Looking forward to taking his class in my upperclassmen years. Go to office hours before a midterm/final and I guarantee you'll ace them.
351 is a hard class and he's easily the best teacher for it.

Professor Martinez-Marquina was hands-down awesome! He's so caring and easy to talk to if you had concerns about your grade or the course content. Lectures are fast-paced for sure, but his office hours are SO worth it! Overall such an amazing professor! He's super accommodating and wants you to succeed in and out of class.
Tests are very similar to practice problems, and lectures are easy to follow. If you show up to class it is very manageable!

Econ 351 is probably one of the hardest classes in Marshall. However, Marquina makes the content very much digestable. He's a very caring professor and wants you to understand the topic, and the lengths that he goes to to do so is very respectable. Genuine guy, very fun to talk to and honestly an amazing professor.

Literally my favorite professor I've taken so far. I would take ANY class he teaches! He was super accessible and reasonable. He genuinely cared for you to grasp the material, and would often stay late after class or office hours if you needed his help.

Yes, lectures are fast paced & the material is difficult. However, Alejandro makes everything manageable. Coming in with no econ experience, I was still able to succeed. To succeed: go to class, read the textbook (its free & really helpful), go to office hours, & do the practice problems (all 3 tests resemble practice problems VERY closely).
great professor with clear lectures, easy homework and tests

Take this class +1 !! Prof. Martinez explains the lectures thoroughly, provides real-world examples, and his pace is perfect. He is determined to help students succeed by going above and beyond to provide office hours (especially before exams) and exam review/revision afterward. Test-heavy, but the content is relevant to lectures and homework.

Amazing professor who truly wants his students to learn and succeed. Grading: 90% from 3 exams, 10% from HW. Thought this course was a very quantitative, fast-paced, and difficult class to get adjusted to. I struggling at first as I failed (D+) both midterm 1 and midterm 2 (post-curve). Got an A on the final exam (post-curve). Ended with a B.

He's a really caring and understanding professor. Although Econ 351 itself can be tough, he makes the lectures engaging and tries his best to help us understand. Doing the homework and practice chapter samples are really helpful for the tests!

Professor Marquina is a very kind and sweet guy. You can tell he genuinely cares for his students, he consistently gave extra office hours and met with me 1-on-1 after my poor 2nd midterm performance, encouraged and strategized with me on how I could improve. 2 midterms & 1 final, very challenging course content. Get ready to put in the work

Take this class!!!!!!! He is such a nice guy and is always willing to meet with students, whether that means just re explaining something after class, holding office hours, or scheduling 1 on 1 time to meet with you and talk through questions or go over tests. If you pay any attention in the lectures you won't have any trouble.

Prof. Martinez is a fairly new professor, but he's one of the best I've had. Although the course is decently tough, if you took AP Econ in Highschool, you'll be fine. Otherwise, he provides very good lectures and is very accessible if you have questions. The hw is harder than the tests, and the practice problems are identical/very similar to tests.

Despite the difficulty of Micro, Professor Martinez-Marquina's lectures are engaging, practical, and interactive. He emphasizes building intuition to see the world from a different perspective and is readily available for support outside of class. Professor Martinez-Marquina's passion and expertise in the subject matter further enrich his lectures.

Thought he was going to be hard since he was new, but ended up being one of the most chill professors I've had. Makes homework harder than the exams, but uses examples similar to slides. Keeps lectures entertaining.

The hardest class at usc, but he makes it worth it. Great professor overall - willing to work with students to help with exams and understanding the material. His lectures go by very fast, and his accent can be hard to understand at first. Go to office hours, read the textbook, pay attention and go to every single class...and maybe you'll pass.

SPAN-290.consensus:
STRENGTHS: Small sample but uniformly positive — 4.5 quality, 2.2 difficulty, 100% would take again. Students describe Prof. Steinberg as passionate, knowledgeable, and fair; essays and reading notes reward engagement with the material.

WORKLOAD: Reading-heavy with regular reading notes plus two essays and two in-class exams (500-point scale). Provisional schedule packs film screenings and primary sources; BrightSpace distributes readings.

BOTTOM LINE: Strong pick for Latin American/Iberian cultural studies if you keep up with readings and take essays seriously. AI use is prohibited — all written work must be your own.

reviews.comment: Prof. Steinberg was engaging during lectures. We were assigned 2 readings per week, and I still passed the class by only attending lectures (no reading). If you follow along in class and take good notes, and refer to the slides him and the TAs post, you'll be in for an easy A and learn a ton!

Be prepared to share a little bit in class about the readings - even if you don't read them. The class was fairly easy, involved some in-class reading quizzes and weekly assignments, but nothing too bad. One in-class midterm and take home final. Somewhat approachable, but overall easy grader.

hands down one of the best professors in the Spanish department. there's a ton of reading but it's worth it; fantastic curation of books, lectures are brilliant and his dry and subtle sense of humor keeps you engaged and laughing. all around wholesome fun that leaves you wishing covid was over so you could take it in person
He's great and speaks perfect Spanish. He isn't harsh if you don't speak perfectly or know every word. He grades pretty easily and I'm surprised I didn't get a solid A. Overall, would take him again.
A lot of reading (books), but lectures are very interesting. He is well-read and knows a lot of literature. Two papers and one presentation but he's an easy grader. Be prepared to discuss the books.

Professor Steinberg is an amazing person and instructor he allows you to voice your opinions but also leads you along the way. He assigns alot of reading but it is totally worth it. Lectures are a must and participation is required but the hard work is worth the trouble.

JS-310.consensus:
STRENGTHS: Very strong RMP profile (4.9 quality, 1.6 difficulty, 100% would take again). Students call Brylak passionate, hilarious, knowledgeable, and caring — one of the best GE picks at USC. Several reviews are explicitly for SLL/JS 310.

WORKLOAD: Heavy reading (~75–100 pp/week per reviews). Weekly reading quizzes (10 questions) are described as easy if you attend lecture; midterm/final quizzes plus two oral presentations (quote analysis + thematic comparison across 3 readings). Physical book required in class; no laptops except for quizzes.

CAVEATS: Oral exams graded on public-speaking standards with follow-up questions. Assignment instructions sometimes vague (older reviews mention papers; current syllabus uses oral exams). Strict attendance — 2 unexcused absences risks failure.

BOTTOM LINE: Engaging instructor and manageable grading if you do the reading and show up; not a phone/laptop class.

reviews.comment: Professor Brylak's SLL-310 is one of the best classes you can take for GE credit. Lectures are extremely engaging and based on the weekly readings, which can be a bit dense but are pretty chill as long as you do them consistently. Grades are based on weekly reading quizzes (very easy) and oral presentations that are honestly pretty fun. Take him!
I love him; he is truly the best. He is so passionate about what he teaches, and he cares for every single student. I recommend him to ANY and EVERYONE.

Had Prof Brylak for SLL 310! Very funny guy but sometimes goes off on confusing tangents. Weekly reading quizzes are very easy, and you honestly don't really have to do the reading to do the quizzes. Also had 2 pretty long papers, and the instructions those were not very clear. Overall, interesting class and he is very knowledgeable and caring!

Cannot recommend prof Brylak more! He is truly an intelligent, caring, and overall amazing teacher. He somehow always has a tidbit of knowledge for whatever tangents we go on and is fantastic at facilitating discussion. He's so engaging, a great presence and I'm very happy I took his class. Assigns ~75-100 pg/week but is a very nice grader!

One of my most fun classes in college. Professor Brylak is energetic, hilarious, and very interesting. The assigned reading and videos are usually interesting. Read and watch them so you do not miss out. His assigned papers are vague, but he is not a difficult grader.

I cannot love this class more!!! Highly recommended!!! Instead of lecturing by himself, he prepares guiding questions for us to discuss and follow our thoughts to deepen in the direction. He is very knowledgeable to answer all of the unexpected tangent questions. A lot of reading but it's worth it, test and final paper are easy.

I took his Easter European Apocalyptic and Post-Apocalyptic Fiction course, and I would highly recommend it. His class is very entertaining and is open to a lot of fun conversation. I had to read around a hundred pages a week and write one page a week, but the weekly papers are graded on completion.

I really enjoyed Professor Brylak's lectures, they were very interesting and I learned a lot from him. We had to read around 100 pages each week and write a one page response paper, but other than that, he is a very easy grader and it made my seminar experience very chill and fun. Take his gesm even if you have no background on the subject!
Professor Brylak knows his stuff and is a very easy grader.

The professor is very passionate about the class, so it is very refreshing to see enthusiasm about the topic. The class itself seems very difficult when looking at the name of the class, but it is actually very interesting and easy. Because the professor is an easy grader, I would consider this class stress-free, interesting, and an easy A.

Great professor! His lectures have a lot of tangents but he's very passionate about the subject so it makes it engaging. A decent amount of reading but easy grading and overall not too much work - a good GESM to take.
Genuinely a sweetheart and loves his classes

I love Dr. Mayfield! She is so easy to talk to and genuinely wants students to do well. Stay on track with the assignments, and ask her for help whenever you need it. I also took ANTH 343 with her, and really enjoyed it! If she taught another class, I would take that one too. Get in her class if you can, you won't regret it!!!

Quite a chill and fair class. Your grade is basically two exams (which are both easy if you keep up with the readings and films) and an essay (which is spread out over several weeks and the topic is your choice). Overall, a laid-back class and an easy A if you put in the effort.
Easy A if you are willing to put into effort. She replied to my emails very quickly. Exams were online and not cumulative. Overall, this is a manageable GE. Definitely recommend!
love her. so passionate and an easy GE.
Not considerate or reasonable. Haphazard assignments, bad communication, and overall not worth your time or effort. Very hard and not even engaging.

Disrespectful, rude, overly demanding/harsh grader. Fail's to prepare enough material for the lectures. Lots of youtube videos and harsh grading. Overall lackluster in terms of being anything worthy of your time or interest. Take something else!

She is so sweet and an amazing prof however do not take this class for an easy A. previous reviews made this class seem very easy and its not. you really have to put the work in. Yes you take your tests at home and they are open note but you really have to know your stuff to succeed. they are not easy. a lot of reading and content to know!

The only reason I rated it as more difficult is because you really do have to put in the work for the class. Others made it sound very easy, but it is not, and she was clear about that from day one. You have weekly at-home quizzes, lots of reading and videos, and attendance is graded! It was a great class but don't expect an easy A.

It is overall not hard to do well in the class. Go to the labs and do all the assigned readings. Professor Mayfield does her best to prepare everyone for the final paper and online exams. She was also very quick to respond to emails and very accessible. With quite a bit to read every week, the difficulty can vary depending on interest in topic.

Overall, Tracie Mayfield is a great professor. If you show up to classes and keep up with the syllabus, you'll probably do fine. However, the class has an insane amount of reading, for frankly a topic that isn't really interesting. Try and get a good lecture time because you have to show up. There's prob better choices but 202 isn't horrible.

If you are looking to take an easy GE, this is by far the best choice. Half the lectures are online and you only have to show up to less than half the lectures. Professor Mayfield is super chill and funny and you will get an A if you complete the course requirements
BEST GE AT USC. All you need is a pulse to get an A. You learn a TON and only need to go to a 50 minute discussion per week. Just follow her directions and you can get a perfect score on everything.

My only complaint is I wish I could have had more class time with Dr. Mayfield! She uses a flipped classroom model where she lectures during discussion (but not every week) and lecture time is like work time. This wasn't the best for me since I enjoy lecture and don't learn as well independently but overall loved the class! She is so caring!
She's so nice and funny one of the best professors for sure

Amazing teacher! Took her for GESM-130. Very passionate about what she teaches. She assigns a midterm, final exam and final project in which she grades leniantly. Attendance isn't mandatory but starts taking points off after 5 absences. Answers emails really well even at 3 AM she will answer your emails. Overall fun, enjoyable easy A.
Great lectures, great person, clear grading rubric and well-defined expectations from class. Would love to take her again!
Not helpful when I need assistance and dismissive

The best GE C you could take. You do have to watch the online lectures and attend the lab sections, but that's all. The midterm and final are open notes, book, google, everything, and are super doable if you take notes on the online lectures and the lab sections' classes. One 7-8 page double spaced paper due in the final week of classes.

Prof Mayfield was amazing. She is so kind, funny, caring, and informative. The class teaches you how to manage your time with the flipped classroom model, but it's manageable once you get a schedule going for yourself. Once a week, mandatory discussions, with the rest being readings and recordings. Definitely easy, but take it for Prof Mayfield!

So grateful I took this class for my GE! Best choice I could've made. Just show up to lab sections and you'll be fine. Professor Mayfield is so caring and attentive to her students, the nicest and most knowledgeable teacher I've had this year. She makes tough concepts easy. Take her!!

Amazing professor! Take. This. Class. Easy A, thoughtful professor, the material is explained very well, and there's one paper you work on throughout the semester (can be as easy as the history of soccer or the history of ice cream).

Literally the nicest human I've ever met. She led my ANTH 201 discussion section, and she was always willing to help us with our essays and other questions. She cares a lot about her students. She prepared us SO WELL for the exams (which are online & open-note). She constantly sends out reminders to help students stay organized and updated.

Amazing professor! Just a great person overall, she is so understandable and flexible. She is so passionate about her studies that it makes you want to excel at all. Do not hesitate to take a Dr. Mayfield course, that is if you are lucky enough to get a spot!

Professor Mayfield is a saint. By far the best professor I've had at USC. Super understanding and flexible with her students but also really knowledgable about the class topics. Taking her class really eased my schedule and allowed me to not get overwhelmed by my others. If you get the chance TAKE ONE OF HER CLASSES.

I really loved her class! Despite being on zoom it was stress free and I genuinely learned a lot! Multiple choice midterm was slightly challenging but that was the only hard thing we did. Weekly quizzes that we could take over and over until we got 100% were dope. She is inspirational and knowledgeable
I really like her! It was hard to engage in class bc of zoom but that wasnt in dr mayfields control. I can see she has a clear passion for what she does.
Really love this professor. Although the content of ANTH201 isn't particularly difficult, Mayfield is passionate about what she teaches. She is very caring and is easy on grading, attendance, etc.

Prof Mayfield is very kind, and cares a lot about her students. Her class gives a good amount of homework, but her lectures were asynchronous (you only have to go to the discussion sections), so there is plenty of time to do the work. There are weekly quizzes with unlimited retakes. She is very clear about what you need to do to get a good grade.
Wonderful teacher with tons of accomplishments under her belt. Tons of opportunities for extra credit and is lenient. Pretty light course load, at least when online.

Great professor online, would love to have her in person. Do the readings and pay attention in discussion and you'll get an A. She makes all assignments, tests, papers very straightforward and is easy to access outside of class.

To be honest, I was not interested in historical archeology, which is the main content taught. The names of the historical sites are hard to memorize, which could be confusing. I don't think I do really well but Mayfield is really nice providing enough chances for you to pass, or to get an A. Not hard to archieve good grades if that's your goal.
Mayfield is like Jesus: if Jesus can turn water into wine Mayfield can turn your grade to be fine

Dr. Mayfield is phenomenal, and 314 is a great GE. If you enjoy history, this class should be pretty easy for you. Lots of extra credit and some pretty fascinating material. Also, the TA Dr. Heller is AMAZING. Dude should be teaching his own course.

Tracie is an absolute gem. Her course material really expanded my understanding of archaeology. She assigns a fair amount of reading per week but it's nothing too difficult or intimidating (imo they're also engaging). As for exams we go over it during class so no stress. You will get a good grade if you do the work. TAKE HER, she's a lovely person!

THE BEST CHOICE FOR AN ONLINE GE! SO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT to keep up and extremely understanding during COVID. No surprises in multiple choice and test (we go over everything) and Professor Mayfield is extremely engaging with students. You can make this class into anything you want it to be, I wrote my final paper around urban studies Take it trust me

Tracie Mayfield is obviously passionate about what she teaches, but she often assigns too much reading every week and expects you to remember tiny details when it comes to the midterm and the final. I enjoyed the subject of the class but it was difficult to keep up. The lectures were also boring and so was the reading.

She is THE BEST!! Super sweet and caring professor, and gives a ton of extra credit opportunities. Weekly quizzes, a midterm, a final, and a paper, but the quizzes were never hard (and you can take them as many times as you wanted). The professor is easily accessible outside of class. Tests were manageable since they were open note. TAKE HER CLASS!

BEST GE PROFESSOR. A lot of work but her caring and on-task personality makes up for it. She provides so many opportunities for extra credit and she is always available outside of class. Although midterm was a little hard, you just gotta review the materials (usually the quizzes and lectures). Course is eh, but the professor is amazing.

She gives a lot of extra credit! Your grade is participation, a 12 page paper, and two exams but the exams are open note and open book. Some of the things we were tested on were pretty random and I would not have done well if it wasn't open book. Mayfield was a casual and engaging lecturer, who really just wants you to be passionate about archaeology. Her lectures and readings had a lot of information, but the exams were all open-book, so it didn't take much work to get an A in the class. ANTH 202's a great GE.

She's great-- knows what she's talking about and how to make you enjoy listening to her. Lots of extra credit, but very few things you get graded on. Basically one final paper and its drafts, along with the final and midterm. Still, an interesting and pretty easy GE.
Awesome professor

Dr. Mayfield made a great TA for ANTH202. Her lab lectures are often group-oriented with fun in-class projects. She has a great habit of treating these projects as a kind of game. Quiz bowls, archaeology case studies, drawing sites, and analyzing pottery shards are all things you'll do.
